content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm having trouble with [product_name] and [product_name]. I'm confused why the marker AM15 and the output for B004 is 34, which is correct, but the output for NAQ1 (memory VW4) is only 3. Thank you for your help!
Your problem is related to overlapping in the VM memory area. VW4 contains VB4 and VB5. VW5 contains VB5 and VB6. To avoid overlap, use NAQ2 with VW6.
Can you elaborate more on this overlapping issue? Thanks!

VM memory addressing is organized by bytes. The smallest unit is a bit; 8 bits make up a byte. Two consecutive bytes (16 bits) make a word, and two consecutive words (4 bytes or 32 bits) form a double word. For example, V0.0 refers to bit 0 in byte 0. VB0 contains bits V0.0 to V0.7. VW0 includes VB0 and VB1 (bits V0.0 to V1.7), and VD0 includes VW0 and VW2 (VB0 to VB3 or V0.0 to V3.7). In bit addresses, the number before the dot is the byte address; the number after is the bit within that byte. For word and double word addresses, the number indicates where the sequence starts. To prevent overlap when working with words, always use even addresses (VW0, VW2, VW4, etc.), and for double words, use multiples of four (VW0, VW4, VW8, etc.).
